grh_cefe06acf56732bd06bd.title: Puppy Love
paragraphs: Blind Peggy Foster leaves her seeing-eye dog Mara with Dr. Christian while she is away, just as the doctor is again dealing with bitter recluse Mrs. Jackson. Since her husband's death years earlier, Mrs. Jackson has shut herself off from neighbors and grown openly hostile toward animals, while pets in the neighborhood have repeatedly disappeared or died. Mara gets loose, crosses near Mrs. Jackson's property and is later found desperately ill and barely able to move. Dr. Christian confronts Mrs. Jackson, who admits putting out poisoned meat to keep animals away and shows little concern for the harm she has caused. He forces her to understand that poisoning Mara is not merely hurting a dog but threatening the independence and freedom of the blind young woman who depends on her. Mara survives treatment. Shaken by Christian's words, Mrs. Jackson recognizes how thoroughly grief has turned her against the world, resolves to become a neighbor again, and volunteers to lead a community collection to buy Dr. Christian a dog of his own as a sign of Rivers End's affection.

grh_ce723440a9f77d1d06eb.title: Tony Donella
paragraphs: On a bitter night Dr. Christian answers a call to the cramped home of Tony and Rosa Donello and finds Rosa critically ill from a ruptured appendix. Rosa is terrified of hospitals because her sister died in one, and Tony has promised she will not be taken away. When the doctor insists that surgery offers her only chance, Tony pulls a gun and orders him to operate in the apartment instead. With Judy boiling water and improvising sterile conditions from whatever they can find, Dr. Christian performs the emergency operation there rather than abandon Rosa. She survives and is later recovering safely, while an overwhelmed Tony offers everything he has in gratitude. The doctor refuses a real fee and keeps one of Tony's barber tools as a souvenir.
